title: A letter of complaint
subtitle: How to demand a solution politely
goal: You can write a 120–150 word letter that describes a problem with a product or a service calmly and demands a specific solution: a refund, a replacement or a repair.
why: An order arrives broken, an airline loses your luggage, a course starts three weeks late. Companies answer letters, and a calm letter with a clear demand is answered faster than an angry message in a chat.
example: Timur bought a phone from a British online shop. It died after three days. His 140-word letter got him a new phone and an apology in a week.
writeTask: Write a letter of complaint (120–150 words) about wireless headphones you bought online: one earphone does not charge, delivery was ten days late, and support has not answered for a week. Say what you bought and when, describe two problems, say what you have already done, demand a solution and give a deadline.

tasks.title: Build the sentence
tasks.howto: Tap the words in the right order — they move into the line. Tap a word in the line to send it back. English word order is fixed, so the order itself carries the meaning.

answers: The laptop that I bought stopped working after a week.
items.why: A relative clause packs two sentences into one.

answers: Could you please send me a new phone?

items.src: The film is good in some ways.
answers: The film is worth watching for its acting, though the plot is weak.
items.why: A review has to commit: say what is good and what is not.

items.src: The phone is faulty. I want a refund.
answers: The phone is faulty; therefore, I would like a refund.
items.why: Therefore is the bridge between evidence and demand.

items.src: The delivery was fast. The phone was broken.
answers: Although the delivery was fast, the phone was broken.
items.why: You admit the good point, then move to the problem.

answers: I would like a full refund.
I would like to request a full refund.
items.why: I want sounds like a demand; I would like is neutral and still firm.
